title: Multimodal AI model predicts cognitive impairment after brain radiotherapy
summary: A gradient-boosted ensemble with attention-based feature fusion combined dosimetric, MRI radiomic (1316 features) and clinical variables from 412 patients at two centers, training on 289 and validating on 123. It reached AUC 0.871 (95% CI 0.821-0.921), above dosimetric-only (0.714), radiomic-only (0.748) and clinical-only (0.682) models, with sensitivity 81.4% and specificity 79.6%.
ai_technology: Gradient-boosted ensemble with attention-based feature fusion on dosimetric, radiomic and clinical features

evidence.tested: Independent validation set of 123 patients from a retrospective two-center cohort.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective; no prospective testing; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning fuses dose, imaging and clinical data to predict impairment at six months.
